Finding high-quality, free 3D assets is one of the best ways to kickstart your game development journey without breaking the bank. 

To help you find exactly what you need, here is a curated list of the best websites and creators for free 3D game assets, categorized by asset style and use case.

---

### 1. The "Big Three" of Free Low-Poly Assets
If you are making a stylized, low-poly, or indie game, these creators are legendary in the game dev community. Almost all of their assets are licensed under **CC0 (Public Domain)**, meaning you can use them in commercial projects without needing to give attribution.

*   **Kenney (kenney.nl):** Known as the "Asset Jesus" of game development, Kenney has released thousands of completely free 3D assets grouped into themed "Kits" (e.g., Space, Castle, Dungeon, Cars, Platformers). They are modular, look great together, and are perfect for rapid prototyping or finished indie games.
*   **Quaternius (quaternius.com):** Quaternius creates incredibly high-quality, free low-poly asset packs. From fully rigged and animated characters (monsters, adventurers, animals) to modular environments (cyberpunk, medieval, nature), all of his packs are CC0 and ready for engines like Unity, Unreal, and Godot.
*   **KayKit (Kay Lousberg on itch.io):** Kay Lousberg makes beautifully stylized, modular low-poly game assets. He offers fantastic character packs (like skeletons and adventurers) that come with built-in animations, alongside dungeon, medieval, and space assets. 

---

### 2. Massive Databases & Asset Repositories
If you need to search for specific objects, these libraries host hundreds of thousands of models.

*   **Poly Pizza (poly.pizza):** This is a dedicated, searchable directory specifically for free low-poly 3D models. It aggregates models from various creators (including Kenney and Quaternius), allowing you to quickly search for terms like "pizza," "sword," or "treasure chest" and download them instantly in formats like FBX, OBJ, or GLTF.
*   **Fab (fab.com):** Launched by Epic Games as a unified marketplace merging the Unreal Engine Marketplace, Sketchfab, ArtStation, and Quixel Megascans. By filtering by **Price: Free**, you can find massive amounts of industry-grade 3D assets, environments, and materials. Additionally, Fab runs "Limited-Time Free" giveaways every two weeks featuring premium asset packs for free.
*   **Sketchfab (sketchfab.com):** A giant community-driven library of 3D models. To find free assets, search for what you want, and make sure to check the **"Downloadable"** filter. You will need to check the license, as many creators use Creative Commons (CC-BY), which requires giving them credit in your game.
*   **Poly Haven (polyhaven.com):** If you are looking for realistic or semi-realistic assets, Poly Haven is unmatched. Everything on the site is 100% free and CC0. It is a goldmine for photorealistic 3D props, high-quality PBR textures, and HDRIs for environment lighting.

---

### 3. Rigging & Animation (Characters)
*   **Mixamo (mixamo.com):** Owned by Adobe, Mixamo is a completely free tool. You can download dozens of premade 3D characters, or upload your own custom humanoid 3D model, use their auto-rigger, and instantly apply hundreds of high-quality, pre-recorded animations (like walking, running, fighting, dancing, and climbing).

---

### 4. General Marketplaces (With Free Filters)
Most of the major commercial 3D marketplaces have substantial "Free" sections to attract developers.

*   **Itch.io (itch.io/game-assets/free/3d):** Itch.io is the home of indie developers. Filtering by "Free" and "3D" will yield thousands of unique, hand-crafted asset packs from solo creators.
*   **CGTrader (cgtrader.com) & TurboSquid (turbosquid.com):** These are massive industry marketplaces for professional 3D artists. By sorting your search results by "Free", you can find highly detailed, professional-grade models for things like realistic weapons, vehicles, and architecture.
*   **Unity Asset Store & Unreal Engine Marketplace (via Fab):** Both engine stores have dedicated free categories containing thousands of high-quality environment kits, templates, and systems. *Note: Some assets acquired from these stores may have licenses restricting their use to that specific engine (e.g., Unreal-only assets).*

---

### ⚠️ A Quick Note on Licensing
Always check the license of a free asset before putting it in a game you intend to release:
*   **CC0 (Public Domain):** Do whatever you want. Commercial use is fine, modification is fine, and no attribution is required.
*   **CC-BY (Attribution):** Free to use commercially, but you **must** credit the creator (usually in your game's credits).
*   **CC-BY-NC (Non-Commercial):** You can only use it for free, non-monetized projects (like game jams or portfolio work). **Do not** use these if you plan to sell your game or put ads in it.
